This is the one-day course on the EU-frames case with open research in the foreground. It works on a study of Eurobarometer surveys, which asked whether the economic crisis changed how citizens of the member states frame the European Union, and on a claim of the original author (OA) that five analysts reanalysed in the Multi100 project. In the morning you meet the arguments and the evidence on the credibility of social science, the three kinds of repetition that go under the word 'replication', the SCORE programme, and the archives, repositories and registries in which the data, code and plans of a study are kept. You then read the paper in full and write the estimand statement behind its claim. In the afternoon you reproduce, to the third decimal, the result that Multi100 recorded for one of the three analysts whose analyses rest on means of countries or of cells, whichever you choose, and you read the code that the analyst deposited for the slip that it carries. You end on the replication that tested the claim on later waves of the survey, and write a preregistration for a replication of the analysis that you reproduced, without running it.

You leave able to tell the three operations of 'replication' apart, to find the deposited materials of a published analysis and read them, and to say what a preregistration fixes and what it leaves open. You also take away a result that you reproduced yourself, an estimand statement for the claim and a preregistration written before any new data were opened. The day has no menu of specifications and sends nothing to a class chart, because the [one-day course on methods](../eu-frames-one-day-methods/index.qmd) does both.

## How you work

The day is taught mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with nothing to install. It works on aggregate data only, the country-year panel of the course and two files that the course rebuilt for two of the analysts, and the lab holds all three. Open it in a tab of its own and keep this page open beside it. Each part of the day has a page that lists its steps in order, and every step that you work at the keyboard has a button that opens the lab at the right task, or the page on which the work is done. If you have installed R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), the downloadable workspace holds the same tasks and gives the same numbers, and the setup page explains how to install it. The slides are on the [slides page](slides.qmd), and each part opens with a link to its place in the deck.

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The class writes its estimand statements, its reproduced values and its rules for a successful replication in the chat and sends them at the same moment, so the day needs a facilitator.

## The parts of the day

- **[Before the day](before.qmd)** (about an hour and a quarter, more with the installation). You read the case study and the exercise overview and open the browser lab once, and you install R, an IDE and the workspace if you want to work there.
- **[Part 1 – Credibility and open research](part-1.qmd)** (ninety minutes). The part asks what a claim is for and why the field talks of a crisis, then covers the three Rs, SCORE and the five analysts of the claim, and the archives, repositories and registries of open research, and it ends with the browser lab running on your machine.
- **[Part 2 – The claim and its estimand](part-2.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after a break of thirty minutes). You read the paper in full, meet estimands and the five questions that the analysts answered, and write the estimand statement in Task 2.
- **[Part 3 – The reproduction](part-3.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after an hour for lunch). You reproduce the recorded result of C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL, find out what the reproduction needed besides the code, and read the code that your analyst deposited for its slip.
- **[Part 4 – Replication and preregistration](part-4.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after a break of thirty minutes). You meet the replication of the claim on new data and what a preregistration fixes, and you write a preregistration for a replication without running it.
- **[After the day](after.qmd)** (as long as you like). The page says where to go next.

[Start with Before the day](before.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

The same case is also taught as one-day courses on [data tools](../eu-frames-one-day-data-tools/index.qmd) and on [methods](../eu-frames-one-day-methods/index.qmd), as a [three-day course](../eu-frames-three-days/index.qmd) that builds the data from the raw survey files, and as a [self-study route](../self-study/index.qmd).
